ledger: Exterior space: two-lane desert highway bordered by sandy scrubland and distant mountains.
Vehicle interior space: vintage wood-paneled station wagon cabin, connected to the exterior view via the front windshield and side windows.

Window views (00:00-00:04): through the front windshield and driver-side windows, the car interior (seats, steering wheel, headrests) and the desert exterior beyond the passenger-side windows are visible.

Occupant placement at vehicle boundary (00:00-00:09): a woman rests her crossed arms on the driver-side front fender/hood edge right at the base of the windshield and in front of the driver-side A-pillar, where only solid vehicle body and engine bay exist.

findings.entity: woman and station wagon front fender/windshield junction
findings.invariant_violated: impossible spatial connectivity between interior and exterior
findings.description: The woman is posed as though leaning out of an opening in the vehicle with her arms resting on the driver-side front fender/hood, but she is positioned forward of the closed driver-side door and A-pillar, with her torso emerging directly out of the solid metal cowl/fender and windshield base where no window, door, or standing space exists.
